tasks.label: OMol
tasks.domain: Aperiodic organic molecules and molecular complexes
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Total charge and spin multiplicity are required model inputs.
official_cautions: Use the OMol task only when molecular charge and spin are defined.

tasks.label: OMC
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Training did not vary charge or spin; the documented inputs are charge=0 and spin multiplicity=0.
official_cautions: Do not treat OMC as a charged-crystal model without validation.

tasks.label: OMat
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Charge and spin are not user-selectable physical states for this task.
official_cautions: OMat total energies are not directly compatible with Materials Project total energies or MP2020 corrections.
Magnetic-state selection is not exposed as a user-controlled condition.

tasks.label: OC20
tasks.reference_method: RPBE with VASP 5.4 pseudopotentials; no dispersion
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Documented inputs are charge=0 and spin multiplicity=0.
official_cautions: OC20 does not cover oxides or explicit solvents.
Transition-state use is described as possible but caution is required.

tasks.label: ODAC
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Documented inputs are charge=0 and spin multiplicity=0.
official_cautions: Training chemistry is centered on CO2/H2O adsorption; hydrocarbons and unseen bare MOFs require caution.

tasks.label: OC25
tasks.reference_method: RPBE+D3 with VASP 6.4 pseudopotentials and dipole corrections
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Training did not explicitly condition on charge or spin.
official_cautions: Available only in UMA 1.2 according to the docs.
Work functions are not model outputs and require subsequent DFT.

tasks.label: OC22
tasks.charge_spin_contract: Documented inputs are charge=0 and spin multiplicity=0.
official_cautions: Available only in UMA 1.2 according to the docs.

datasets.label: OMol25
datasets.role: Molecular quantum chemistry training and evaluation
datasets.license_note: Check the dataset card; repository license does not automatically cover payloads.

datasets.label: OMol25 Electronic
datasets.role: Electronic-property extension of the molecular domain

datasets.label: OMat24
datasets.role: Large-scale inorganic training data and Matbench-compatible discovery evaluation
datasets.license_note: The documentation identifies CC BY 4.0 for OMat24; model licenses remain separate.

datasets.label: ODAC25
datasets.role: Expanded DAC benchmark and model domain

technologies.label: UMA with Mixture of Linear Experts
technologies.what_it_does: Shares an equivariant backbone across chemistry domains while routing task, charge, spin and composition information through expert modules.
technologies.paper_use: Explain why a single model can expose multiple DFT-task identities without pretending those identities are interchangeable.

technologies.label: pretrained_mlip model loader
technologies.what_it_does: Resolves named checkpoints and returns a prediction unit for a selected task.
technologies.paper_use: Record model ID, task ID, checkpoint source and package version with every result.

technologies.label: FAIRChemCalculator
technologies.what_it_does: Exposes MLIP energies, forces and stress through the ASE calculator interface.
technologies.paper_use: Connect official inference to relaxations, MD and property workflows while preserving task metadata.

technologies.label: Batch and Ray inference
technologies.what_it_does: Runs batched model inference and supports distributed workers for larger structure collections.
technologies.paper_use: Useful for screening throughput, but batching does not create statistical independence or scientific validity.

technologies.label: InferenceBatcher
technologies.what_it_does: Collects multiple requests into efficient inference batches.
technologies.paper_use: A possible service layer for a future webapp queue, separate from the evidence database.

technologies.label: ASE-readable datasets
technologies.what_it_does: Provides ASE-file, multi-structure and ASE-DB readers plus LMDB-oriented data tooling.
technologies.paper_use: A reference for normalizing structures and labels before fine-tuning or evaluation.

technologies.label: Configuration-driven training
technologies.what_it_does: Builds MLIP training runs from reusable model, data, optimizer and task configurations.
technologies.paper_use: Keep the complete configuration and split policy as provenance; do not report only the checkpoint name.

technologies.label: Evaluation workflows
technologies.what_it_does: Runs configured evaluation jobs and benchmark reducers.
technologies.paper_use: Use chemistry-grouped, task-matched evaluation instead of interpreting random row splits as transfer performance.

technologies.label: Fine-tuning
technologies.what_it_does: Adapts a pretrained model using project-specific labeled structures.
technologies.paper_use: For LPSCl, fine-tune only after DFT labels, split policy and target conventions are frozen.

technologies.label: Composable calculate workflows
technologies.what_it_does: Provides runners and recipes for single points, relaxations and derived properties.
technologies.paper_use: Separate input generation, execution, collection and approval in our own workflow contract.

technologies.label: Geometry relaxation
technologies.what_it_does: Relaxes atomic positions and, when requested, cell degrees of freedom.
technologies.paper_use: Report optimizer, force/stress convergence and maximum steps; model output alone is not convergence.

technologies.label: ASE molecular dynamics
technologies.what_it_does: Runs MD with thermostat and trajectory utilities.
technologies.paper_use: Distinct trajectories require explicit, recorded random seeds; preserve raw trajectories needed by retrospective gates.

technologies.label: LAMMPS integration
technologies.what_it_does: Connects FAIR-Chem inference to LAMMPS workflows.
technologies.paper_use: Potential route for larger MD after ASE-level equivalence and reproducibility checks.

technologies.label: Elastic-property workflow
technologies.what_it_does: Generates strained structures and evaluates elastic response.
technologies.paper_use: Specify relaxed-ion versus clamped-ion semantics and reject nonphysical moduli before aggregation.

technologies.label: Phonon workflow
technologies.what_it_does: Builds force-constant/phonon calculations around MLIP forces.
technologies.paper_use: Use as a stability diagnostic only after supercell and displacement convergence checks.

technologies.label: Thermal-conductivity workflow
technologies.what_it_does: Provides a recipe and benchmark runner for lattice thermal conductivity workflows.
technologies.paper_use: Do not confuse this capability with ionic conductivity; the observables and validation are different.

technologies.label: Formation-energy workflow
technologies.what_it_does: Combines predicted energies with task-specific elemental references.
technologies.paper_use: Keep OMat reference energies and corrections isolated from Materials Project energy conventions.

technologies.label: AdsorbML
technologies.what_it_does: Accelerates adsorption-energy searches using ML relaxations plus higher-level evaluation.
technologies.paper_use: A pattern for coarse-to-expensive screening, not a directly transferable solid-electrolyte gate.

technologies.label: CatTSunami
technologies.what_it_does: Builds transition-state workflows for catalytic surface reactions.
technologies.paper_use: Borrow workflow ideas only; bulk-Li hopping has a different system and method contract.

technologies.label: FastCSP
technologies.what_it_does: Accelerates molecular crystal structure prediction.
technologies.paper_use: Relevant as a search/relax/rerank architecture, not as a chemistry-equivalent model for LPSCl.

technologies.label: OCx application tools
technologies.what_it_does: Connects catalyst experiment data and modeling workflows.
technologies.paper_use: A useful precedent for keeping experimental and computational evidence linked but not merged.

technologies.label: Generative structure models
technologies.what_it_does: The documentation indexes several diffusion, flow-matching and language-model approaches for structure generation.
technologies.paper_use: Potential future candidate generator; every generated structure still needs domain and stability validation.

technologies.label: Benchmark reducers
technologies.what_it_does: Aggregates task-specific benchmark outputs for discovery, adsorption, molecular and speed tests.
technologies.paper_use: Reuse the idea of task-specific reducers; never force unrelated properties into one universal score.

claims.statement: Fair-Chem v2 is a breaking redesign rather than an in-place continuation of the v1 trainer/calculator stack.
claims.caveat: Pin major version and migration assumptions in all project provenance.

claims.statement: Pretrained checkpoints are fetched from gated Hugging Face repositories and require license acceptance/authentication.
claims.caveat: Repository MIT licensing does not imply identical licensing for every model or dataset.

claims.statement: UMA task labels encode different data domains and electronic-structure conventions; they are not interchangeable application tags.
claims.caveat: Record task ID with every value and never pool energies across tasks without an explicit bridge.

claims.statement: OMat/UMA total energies are not directly compatible with Materials Project total energies or MP2020 corrections.
claims.caveat: Do not mix UMA-OMat energies into MP hull or grand-potential tables as if they shared a reference.

claims.statement: The prediction-unit construction path sets a global NumPy seed, so independent MD trajectories need explicitly distinct seeds.
claims.caveat: A different directory label is not evidence of an independent stochastic trajectory.

claims.statement: At the pinned source commit, OC22 is documented as a UMA 1.2 task but is absent from the public UMATask enum.
claims.caveat: Recheck on upgrade; do not present this snapshot observation as a permanent product limitation.

claims.statement: The code-registered pretrained model inventory can be newer or broader than models highlighted in prose documentation.
claims.caveat: Show docs-advertised and code-registered states separately in the webapp.

claims.statement: Availability of a relaxation, MD, elasticity, phonon or fine-tuning workflow does not validate that workflow for a new chemistry or observable.
claims.caveat: Store capability, project validation and approved use as separate fields.

claims.statement: Batch inference improves throughput but does not turn multiple inputs into controlled replicates or concentration points.
claims.caveat: Experimental-design identity must come from structure/composition/seed provenance.

claims.statement: The FAIR Chemistry papers page is a curated index, not proof that every method is suitable for LPSCl.
claims.caveat: Each paper added to litdb still needs figure inspection and an explicit comparison-vs-ours note.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_use: LPSCl structural relaxation, screening and selected MD
lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Use the project-pinned model/task/protocol. Official support does not override the Li3N ban or convergence gates.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: UMA provides an inorganic pretrained potential used as a computational accelerator; project-specific validation defines the claim scope.

lpscl_crosswalk.fairchem_capability: OMat total energy and formation-energy references
lpscl_crosswalk.project_use: Host-relative energies within one frozen protocol
lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Do not merge OMat energies with Materials Project hull/grand-potential values. Keep method_id and reference set explicit.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: MLIP energy differences were interpreted only within the same task and reference convention.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Persist fmax, step count, residual stress, optimizer, model version and final structure. A returned structure is not automatically converged.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Structures were relaxed with a pinned UMA/OMat calculator and promoted only after explicit force/stress convergence checks.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Use the project canonical temperature/seed/time-window contract and save raw trajectories required by retrospective gates.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: FAIR-Chem supplied the force engine; trajectory generation, seed policy and transport estimator followed the project protocol.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Record strain/relaxation semantics and reject non-positive or otherwise nonphysical moduli before species aggregation.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Elastic quantities were treated as configuration-conditional diagnostics, not intrinsic values until convergence and validity checks passed.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Require displacement, supercell and force-convergence studies before promotion.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Phonons remain a planned validation layer rather than an output of the current screen.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Use a separately pinned Materials Project phase set for MP thermodynamics; never substitute UMA/OMat totals into that ledger.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Thermodynamic phase competition was evaluated in a method-specific external phase-set workflow, separate from UMA screening energies.

lpscl_crosswalk.fairchem_capability: Catalysis transition-state tooling and general MLIP forces
lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: CatTSunami/OC20NEB are catalysis-specific. Bulk Li hopping requires our own cell, path and DFT validation contract.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: MLIP barriers were used only to scout paths; absolute barriers required matched DFT validation.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: Batch records need immutable composition, site, seed and method identity. Throughput metadata must not be used as a replicate label.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Batched inference reduced computational cost, while scientific denominators were defined from exact structure provenance.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: First fix relaxation convergence and collect composition-diverse DFT energies/forces/stress; use nested chemistry-group evaluation.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Fine-tuning is reserved for residual systematic error after protocol defects are removed.

lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: UMA is banned for Li3N by project evidence even though the official task is broad.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: Li3N was excluded from UMA-based claims under a project-specific validation decision.

lpscl_crosswalk.fairchem_capability: Named pretrained model registry and versioned releases
lpscl_crosswalk.project_rule: A model/version upgrade creates a new method_id. Do not silently mix UMA 1.1 and 1.2 values.
lpscl_crosswalk.paper_language: All model upgrades were treated as method changes and benchmarked before data pooling.
